title: A town laid out by the railroad
text: During World War II, several local women in Mojave worked for the Southern Pacific maintaining locomotives in the railroad's roundhouse. The railroad established a yard in Mojave and made it a division point. The railroad also laid out the town, and its layout and street names were still in use after 135 years. Wind turbine components now move from rail cars to trucks at the Mojave Air and Space Port.
